projects.title: Prismet
projects.subtitle: A calm home for classic games, on iPhone, iPad, and Mac
projects.role: Product, design, iOS + macOS engineering, release
projects.summary: Nineteen classic games and three live-data lenses in one app, each game with its own hand-built look. Chess plays a tunable Stockfish engine in 2D or 3D, the Rubik's Cube is a real SceneKit cube, and friends can play Sea Battle, Checkers, Reversi, Connect Four, and Gomoku online. The Mac app ships at feature parity with iOS.
highlights: Shipped v1.0 to the App Store; v1.1 rebrand submitted with saves and Game Center continuity preserved
Daily Wordgame fed by a self-hosted endpoint on prismet.xyz
Light, parchment, and dark reading themes; sound and haptics on every move
Built with a team of AI agents under a written coordination protocol (see Agent Ops)

projects.title: The Wizard King's Decree
projects.subtitle: Can chat models call the news before it happens?
projects.summary: A council of two chat models must agree on a no-hedge prophecy about upcoming news. A separate, search-grounded Court Historian grades each decree against reality with at least two independent sources, and wrong calls trigger public corrections on an escalating ladder. Under the robes it is an auditable forecasting experiment with hit rates, bootstrap confidence intervals, and calibration.
highlights: Every SDK, clock, and network call sits behind an injectable seam, so the whole suite runs with no keys and no network
Append-only rulings and corrections in SQLite
Static-site chronicle generated with the standard library only

projects.title: Bayzyl
projects.subtitle: An in-game building toolkit for Paper servers
projects.summary: Selections, shapes, brushes, clipboards, persistent undo, shared kits, and builder profiles, in one consistent command set. Every option uses option:value syntax, tab-completion knows about masks and block distributions, and big edits ask for confirmation first. It runs alongside WorldEdit and FastAsyncWorldEdit, and falls back to its own implementations when neither is installed.
highlights: Per-player undo history that survives restarts, plus /oops to undo and tell the team
Shared builder kits with themes, icons, aliases, and notes
Formula-driven /generate and /generatebiome
Quality-of-life tools: ghost hand, auto-unstick, ruler, surface/ascend/descend

projects.title: Minecraft server network
projects.subtitle: A Velocity proxy, Dockerized Paper backends, and one admin command
projects.summary: A multi-server network: a Velocity proxy handles login, whitelisting, and network-wide bans, while containerized Paper backends run a multi-world survival server and a public hub. A single mc-admin command routes every task to the layer where it belongs, so an IP ban never lands on a backend and locks out the proxy.
facts: one CLI for whitelist, bans, ops, gamerules, RCON
highlights: Whitelist by Mojang UUID, resolved automatically from a player name
Per-world gamerules through Multiverse
Escape hatches straight to the proxy console or backend RCON

projects.title: QR Scanner & pocket tools
projects.subtitle: One-file web tools that never phone home
projects.summary: A QR scanner that runs from a single HTML file with no backend and no build step, plus three siblings: a phone declutter checklist with 46 tasks across 11 zones, a home-screen planner that sorts 300+ apps into verb-named folders on a live phone mockup, and an Apple Music playlist maker built on your real listening history.
highlights: Native BarcodeDetector first, vendored jsQR fallback everywhere else
Progress and plans saved on-device only

projects.title: Steam Rewind & Debt Clock
projects.subtitle: Live-data lenses on the web and in the app
projects.summary: Two lenses that started in the Prismet app and now live on prismet.xyz. Steam Rewind reads a Steam library and turns playtime into a story. The Debt Clock ticks the U.S. national debt from Treasury data, with a smoothed growth rate and a live up/down banner.
highlights: Same engine on iOS, macOS, and the web

projects.title: PrismCode
projects.subtitle: Mission control for Claude Code, Codex, and DeepSeek
projects.summary: A desktop IDE where three coding agents work side by side over one workspace, each normalized into a single event stream. PRISM A/B races Claude against Codex on the same prompt in separate git worktrees, then diffs the results so you keep the winner. Sessions resume, accounts hot-swap, and a usage tracker shows spend per account.
highlights: One adapter per agent, one AgentEvent contract: adding an agent needed no UI work
Git worktree racing with compare, apply-winner, and keep-both
Zero-token dev loop with a mock agent

projects.title: Agent Ops
projects.subtitle: How a family ships software with a team of AI agents
projects.summary: A written contract every agent reads first: who owns which lane, how to claim files in a shared ledger, how to sync through git, and which build rules are non-negotiable. It let several Claude and Codex agents, run by two people, ship an App Store release without trampling each other's work.
highlights: Lane claims and releases logged in a coordination ledger
Release gates tracked in one file

projects.title: THE HELM
projects.subtitle: A red-on-black command bridge for a three-monitor Linux desktop
projects.summary: A full desktop system built on KDE Plasma 6: 28 native QML widgets for telemetry, network, storage, and arcade games, fullscreen app overlays, floating toys, a live packet scope, and a widget locker that docks and deploys faces on command. One helm command drives everything, and a written design-language spec keeps every face consistent.
highlights: Faces render standalone with sample data, so every widget can be previewed and screenshotted headless
Shared chrome and palette tokens synced into every widget
Arcade faces (Breakout, Minesweeper, Snake, Orbital Defense) next to CPU, GPU, and fleet telemetry

projects.title: Quark
projects.subtitle: A personal hub for mail, school, code, and files
projects.summary: One window with a tab strip for every service in a busy week, each tab in its own isolated session so sign-ins never collide. Sign-ins persist across restarts, saved credentials live in an OS-encrypted vault, and a built-in Files tab edits a shared local workspace.
highlights: All views stay attached, so captchas and WebGL keep rendering when you switch tabs
